supporting_observations.claim: WS-NKIM-01 made repeated proxy CONNECT requests to update.casebinder.com:443 at approximately five-minute intervals: 13:42, 13:47, 13:52, 13:57, 14:02, 14:07, and 14:11 UTC.

The CaseBinder updater process was observed running on WS-NKIM-01 and initiating connections through the proxy to the approved CaseBinder update service, supporting that it generated the periodic activity.
The observed proxy connections succeeded and were short-lived; the proxy logged status 200 and durations of seconds.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records CONNECT tunnel metadata, not the encrypted HTTPS content, requested paths, or update payload.
The evidence ties the recurring CaseBinder connections to the updater process from 13:42 UTC onward; it does not show a corresponding CaseBinder connection at the beginning of the alert window.
The available records do not establish the updater binary's signature, hash, or integrity.
claims_not_established: The records do not establish what content was exchanged inside the encrypted CaseBinder HTTPS tunnels.
The records do not establish whether every connection described by the alert is represented in the supplied telemetry.
unrelated_findings: A separate proxy CONNECT to docs.google.com:443 occurred at 13:30:34 UTC; it is not the recurring CaseBinder activity and should be reviewed separately against the organization's approved-services policy (T166-00051).

A Dropbox updater executable ran briefly as SYSTEM; Dropbox is not listed among approved services, and this execution is not tied by the supplied records to the alerted periodic connections (T166-00227, T166-00230, T166-00231).

WS-NKIM-01 made SMB connections to DC-MAP-01 during the review window; these are separate from the alerted HTTPS activity and may warrant contextual review (T166-00079, T166-00083, T166-00292, T166-00296).
